newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia in talks over $70 mln IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia in talks over $70 mln IMF loan.

text.p: The former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia is negotiating a three to five year funding arrangement of up to $70 million with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a central banker said on Friday.

"We are in preliminary talks with an IMF mission now in Skopje over a reform funding programme of between $50 million and $70 million," the banker, who declined to be named, told Reuters by telephone.
Maintaining a steady exchange rate and low inflation, adoption of a new tax system and upgrading the public sector by setting up pension funds are the main reform targets, said the official.

Completing sell-offs of state enterprises and stabilising the banking sector are also part of the funding requirements under the Extended Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF), which will be negotiated over the next few weeks.

The country has received a total of $75 million from the IMF between 1993 and mid-1996 and a total of $260 million in World Bank project funding and structural adjustment loans. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
